# <span id="aanchor61"></span> Query Editor

The Query Editor allows a user to create a query to run against the FLOWCAL database. The user can also edit an existing query and create a new query based on an existing query. Queries can be used for filtering out objects (e.g., meters, locations, sources) and as the basis for Dynamic Lists.

A query can be executed for all meters, a meter list, a location, all source analyses, or a source analysis list. The query will run for all dates by default, but can be applied to a specific date range.

<div class="procedure">

To access the Query Editor: 

- Go to **Tools** \> **Query Editor**; or
- Click the **Query** button in the List Editor when creating a dynamic list.



<img src="data:image/png;base64," class="ScreenShot" style="width: 566;height: 432;" />

For a list of possible values for the most commonly used tables and fields, see the [Query Cheat Sheet](Query%20Cheat%20Sheet.md).

</div>

<a href="javascript:void(0);" class="MCToggler MCTogglerHead MCTogglerHotSpot MCToggler_Open toggler MCTogglerHotSpot_ MCHotSpotImage" data-mc-targets="Details">

<img src="data:image/gif;base64," class="MCToggler_Image_Icon" data-mc-alt2="Open" width="16" height="11" alt="Closed" />Query Editor Screen Details</a>

<div class="drop-down" style="display: none;" mc-target-name="Details">

The following items are available on the Query Editor screen:

- **Query Name** - Click the drop-down to select an existing query. Queries for all object types (e.g., meter, location, source) will be listed.
- **Meters, Locations, Sources** - Reflects the object type associated with the Query Name selected.
- **SQL** - Show the SQL compiled based on the query options selected.
- **New** - Create a new query.
- **Copy** - Create a copy of a selected query.
- **Edit** - Edit an existing query.
- **Run** - Run an existing query. A Query Results screen will appear showing the results of the query.
- **Delete** - Delete a query.
- **OK** - Exit the form.
- **Cancel** - Cancel edits and do not save changes.

</div>

<a href="javascript:void(0);" class="MCToggler MCTogglerHead MCTogglerHotSpot MCToggler_Open toggler MCTogglerHotSpot_ MCHotSpotImage" data-mc-targets="Tabs">

<img src="data:image/gif;base64," class="MCToggler_Image_Icon" data-mc-alt2="Open" width="16" height="11" alt="Closed" />Query Editor Tab Details</a>

<div class="drop-down" style="display: none;" mc-target-name="Tabs">

The Query Editor includes three sub-tabs:

- **Criteria** - Displays the tables/columns, operands, values, dates, etc. used as the criteria for the query. Up to 15 criteria are supported.  
  <a href="javascript:void(0);" class="MCToggler MCTogglerHead MCTogglerHotSpot MCToggler_Open toggler MCTogglerHotSpot_ MCHotSpotImage" data-mc-targets="Criteria Details">

<img src="data:image/gif;base64," class="MCToggler_Image_Icon" data-mc-alt2="Open" width="16" height="11" alt="Closed" />Sub-Tab Details</a>
  <div class="drop-down" style="display: none;" mc-target-name="Criteria Details">

  - **Table** - Used to filter the type of data to query for. The Table drop-down is populated based on the query object type selected (e.g. Meters, Locations, Sources).
  - **Field** - Used to select the field to query against. The Field drop-down is populated based on the Table selected.
  - **Operand** - Used to select the operand to use in the criteria (e.g. \<, \>, =, \<\>). The Query Editor supports Match and Skip operators for Equal and Not Equal using exact numbers or strings.
  - **Value** - Contains the values to query for. Wild card characters of "\*" and "%” are also supported.
  - **\*** - The "\*" column indicates whether the Value is case sensitive - checked means exact value, unchecked means that case does not matter. For numeric values such as pressure base, unchecking the field will cause FLOWCAL to round the value to the number of decimal places specified.
  - **And/Or** - Used to include more than one criterion in the query. When And is used, the value must meet both criteria to be true. When Or is used, the value must meet one or the other to be true.
  - **For All Date, Date/Time, Data Set Dates** - The query will run for all dates by default, but can be applied to a specific date range.

  </div>
- **Sort By** - The query results will return in order by object number, such as meter number. Use the Sort By tab to select one or more fields to sort the results by.
- **Selection Pool** - By default, the query will run against all objects. To limit the query pool, select an option from the Selection Pool. For example, for a meter query, the user can select a list of meters to run the query against.

</div>

<a href="javascript:void(0);" class="MCToggler MCTogglerHead MCTogglerHotSpot MCToggler_Open toggler MCTogglerHotSpot_ MCHotSpotImage" data-mc-targets="Results">

<img src="data:image/gif;base64," class="MCToggler_Image_Icon" data-mc-alt2="Open" width="16" height="11" alt="Closed" />View Query Results</a>

<div class="drop-down" style="display: none;" mc-target-name="Results">

You can view the results of a selected query or a query as it is being created.

<div class="procedure">

To view query results:

1.  From the Query Editor, click the **Run** button. The Query Results screen will open with the results.
2.  Click **OK** to close.



<img src="data:image/png;base64," class="ScreenShot" style="width: 408;height: 359;" />

</div>

</div>

<a href="javascript:void(0);" class="MCToggler MCTogglerHead MCTogglerHotSpot MCToggler_Open toggler MCTogglerHotSpot_ MCHotSpotImage" data-mc-targets="Printing">

<img src="data:image/gif;base64," class="MCToggler_Image_Icon" data-mc-alt2="Open" width="16" height="11" alt="Closed" />Print Query Results</a>

<div class="drop-down" style="display: none;" mc-target-name="Printing">

You can print query results for a selected query or a query as it is being created.

<div class="procedure">

To print query results:

1.  From the Query Editor, click the **Run** button. The Query Results screen will open with the results.
2.  Click the **Select All** button to select all the objects returned in the query results. All objects appearing on the right side of the form will be printed.
3.  Click the **Print** button to see the report displaying the query and the query results.

The report always prints the selected objects ordered by their unique identifier (meter number, quality source number, or location number). It does not use the Sort By criteria specified in the report.



<img src="data:image/png;base64," class="ScreenShot" style="width: 407;height: 360;" />

</div>

</div>
